title: ⭐⭐ Revision: what was promised, what happened

questions.prompt: A manager sums up a guest's file, but his five sentences have been shuffled. Put them back in the order in which the events happened.

options.text: She landed at midnight and waited two hours for a taxi.
She chose the trip from our brochure in the spring.
She wrote to us the day after she got home.
She paid a deposit that week and booked the holiday.
She paid the balance thirty days before departure.

questions.explanation: A holiday is bought in a fixed order, and the words of the counter name its stages. You choose from the brochure; you pay a deposit, and only then does the booking exist; you pay the balance, the rest of the price, before the date printed in the conditions — nobody flies with a balance unpaid. Then comes the holiday itself, with whatever goes wrong in it. And the letter of complaint comes last: it is written once the guest is home, which is why everything in it has to be reported rather than said.

questions.prompt: Tick EVERY word below whose main stress falls on the FIRST syllable.

options.text: booking
excursion
interested
superb
recommend

questions.explanation: BOOK-ing and IN-ter-est-ed both open on their loudest syllable, and length changes nothing: a four-syllable word can perfectly well be stressed at its beginning. Two other words of the same lesson do not follow: ex-CUR-sion and su-PERB carry the stress on their second syllable. And rec-om-MEND keeps it for the third and last, which is why the word sounds as if it were rushing towards its end.

questions.prompt: An airport screen prints: "Flight TU 714 — scheduled 07.45 — expected 11.20". What is it telling the passengers?

options.text: the flight is more than three hours late
the flight will now leave earlier than planned
the flight has been cancelled for the day
the flight leaves at a quarter to eight

questions.explanation: Scheduled means planned, printed on the timetable — that is the time the flight was always supposed to leave. Expected is the time it will really go. When the expected time comes after the scheduled one, the gap between the two is the delay, and from 07.45 to 11.20 that gap is three hours and thirty-five minutes. Reading the scheduled time as the real one is exactly the mistake the screen is trying to prevent, and a cancelled flight is given no expected time at all.

questions.prompt: You are writing to the manager of the hotel, not speaking to him at the desk. Which opening line belongs in a letter of complaint?

options.text: Hi there! Just a quick word about that room you gave us.
I am writing to complain about the room we were given last week.
I am writing to say how much we enjoyed the room you gave us.
Could you tell me whether the room we were given last week is free?

questions.explanation: A written complaint opens with a formula worth learning by heart: I am writing to complain about, followed straight away by its subject. The formula itself is neutral — the same opening carries thanks when you write to say how much you enjoyed something — so it is the verb that does the work, and choosing the wrong one turns your letter into the opposite of what you meant. A cheerful greeting belongs to a message to a friend, and asking whether the room is free is an enquiry, which does not complain about anything.

questions.prompt: A hotel's web page has a heading "Facilities". Which line belongs under that heading?

options.text: the price of a double room in July
the date of your arrival and departure
a swimming pool, a gym and a car park
the name of the agency that sold the trip

questions.explanation: Facilities are the things a hotel puts at the disposal of its guests — equipment and services they can use once they are inside. Prices belong under a heading of their own, usually rates or tariffs; the dates of arrival and departure belong to your own booking and change with every guest; and the name of the agency appears on the voucher, not on the hotel's page. The question matters at the moment of complaining: a facility that is advertised and then closed is a promise that has been broken.

questions.prompt: Marion's package included three excursions. None of them took place, but the flight and the hotel were exactly as promised. What can she reasonably ask the agency for?

options.text: the whole price of her package holiday
a free holiday at the same hotel next year
the deposit she paid when she booked the trip
the money she paid for the three excursions

questions.explanation: The fourth move of a complaint asks for what matches what was lost. Three excursions were paid for and never delivered, so their price is the sum the agency owes, and it is the only claim it cannot argue about. Asking for the whole package means asking to be paid back for a flight she took and a hotel she slept in. A free holiday is far bigger than the loss, and a claim bigger than the loss lets the agency discuss the claim instead of the loss. And the deposit is not an extra sum: it is the first part of the price she agreed to pay.
